content:
Crews are back at work at the fire-damaged DoubleTree hotel in downtown Laredo, where private engineering teams have begun putting up large steel beams to stabilize the structure, Mayor Victor Treviño told KGNS.

The work is the next step in a stabilization effort officials have said could take five to six weeks. Until it is done, local, state and federal investigators still cannot go inside to look for a cause, because of collapse risks.

The three-alarm fire broke out in the early hours of October 7 at the 14-story hotel at 800 Garden Street. Engineers identified significant damage to structural columns on the fifth floor, where the fire is believed to have started, raising concerns that the building could partially or totally collapse.

Mayor Treviño has declined to issue a new emergency declaration after the most recent one expired October 23, shifting the recovery from emergency city orders to private stabilization work. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is assisting in the investigation.

Nearby businesses, including the Don Vicente restaurant and the Courtyard hotel, continue to face restricted customer traffic from road closures around the safety perimeter, and the Laredo Christmas parade route was changed because of the site.

No cause has been determined, and no reopening date — or final decision on repair versus demolition — has been announced.

What to watch

The steel-beam work is the first visible sign of progress since the fire, but the key questions remain unanswered: what caused the blaze, how long the perimeter stays up, and whether the building can be saved at all. Webb Watch will keep following the stabilization timeline and the investigation.
